s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive cutaneous eruption with hyperkeratotic papules
salient_findings: Reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules on the left leg
Slight bleeding after removal of scales
Compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate on biopsy
key_facts: 10-year history of slowly progressive cutaneous eruption
Eruption located on the front and back of the left leg
Papules are 1 to 10 mm wide
Patient has a 16-year history of diabetes mellitus
Diabetes is being treated with metformin
No history of another endocrine disorder or malignant neoplasm
No family history of similar cutaneous findings
Hematological and biochemical test results are unremarkable
Lesional skin biopsy shows compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate and epidermal atrophy are characteristic features

shortlist.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: presence of hyperkeratotic papules and lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lichenoid keratosis
shortlist.why_kept: clinical and histological features overlap with lichen planus, but this is a distinct entity to consider

shortlist.label: Psoriasis
shortlist.why_kept: hyperkeratotic papules and absence of other systemic symptoms make this a plausible diagnosis

shortlist.label: Granuloma faciale
shortlist.why_kept: although less common, the presence of hyperkeratotic papules and lymphocyte infiltrate make this a possible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The clinical presentation of reddish brown hyperkeratotic papules and the histopathological findings of compact hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and bandlike lymphocyte infiltrate are consistent with lichenoid keratosis, especially given the solitary and localized nature of the eruption.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: Lichen planus typically presents with multiple lesions and often involves the mucous membranes, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Discoid lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Discoid lupus erythematosus usually presents with atrophic scarring lesions and is often associated with other systemic or cutaneous manifestations of lupus, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Psoriasis
rejected.why: Psoriasis typically presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales, and the histopathological findings do not match those described in the case.

rejected.label: Granuloma faciale
rejected.why: Granuloma faciale is a rare condition that typically presents with brownish plaques on the face, which does not match the location or description of the eruption in this case.
